identity_assessment.basis: The preferred working identification is that George Glasgw in Mureistoun in the 1586 Calder muster obligation was the adult George Glasgow who witnessed the 17 February 1605 baptism of George, son of James Glasgow in provisionally read Muirestoun. The 1605 household points to the same holding as the earlier George, within the same parish setting. The surname is specific to this local comparison, and a 19-year interval is straightforward for one adult career. A child bearing George’s name and an adult George participating in his baptism make a continuing local family association more economical than two unconnected Georges. Together these observations warrant probable rather than merely possible cross-record identity. They do not amount to independent proofs of every step.
identity_assessment.limitations: The witness’s own residence is unstated, and another George in the district remains possible. The residence reading Muirestoun and its identification as Murieston remain probable. Shared spelling and locality are related observations; McCall repeats Maidment’s 1586 act and is not a second muster occurrence. Naming the child George is supporting context, not proof of a naming rule. The 1586 act records an obligation, not attendance. Neither source gives George’s age or states a relationship to James. Father, uncle, brother, other kinsman and neighbour remain alternatives. No father is changed: Andrew Glasgow-3163 remains James’s selected uncertain father, while George is an important competing paternal or collateral explanation. George Glasgow-1099, the merchant, remains compatible but unselected; the 1586 minor’s curatorship and the 1598 marriage contract do not identify him at Murieston. No mother, birth date, identity merge or confidently marked paternal edge is added.

prior_assessment.status: HOLD — possible same man; kinship unresolved
prior_assessment.identity_note: The original Mid Calder baptism of 17 February 1605 names father James Glasgow, provisionally in Muirestoun, and adult witness George Glasgow. The 1586 Calder muster list names George Glasgw in Mureistoun. Murieston is the probable common locality; the two older George occurrences may be one man, but no kinship is stated.
prior_assessment.minimum_fields: George; surname Glasgw/Glasgow; male as the muster subject and adult baptism witness. Recorded at Mureistoun in 1586; possible witness at Mid Calder in 1605. Birth, death, parents, spouse and children unknown. Murieston is a probable locality identification, not an exact palaeographic reading.
